title: One plugin, called emzakit
summary: The local mundhir-principles skill, rules, agents and hooks become one plugin named emzakit; the workflow is /emzakit:principles.
decision: The skill, the rules file, the four agents and the two hooks that lived in ~/.claude are packaged as one Claude Code plugin in the repo emzakit/emzakit_claude_adhd. Plugin and marketplace are both named emzakit; the skill is named principles.
reason: One install on any machine instead of five hand-copied pieces.
alternatives: Keeping the name mundhir-principles; a plugin named after the repo.

title: The rules arrive through hooks
summary: RULES.md is injected by one hook script on SessionStart and SubagentStart, because a plugin cannot install a file into ~/.claude/rules and SessionStart context never reaches subagents.
decision: hooks/inject_context.py prints skills/principles/RULES.md as additional context on SessionStart and on SubagentStart. On SessionStart it also prints the record digest and any missing companion plugins.
reason: The rules must be in force in every session and every subagent without a second copy to keep in step.
alternatives: An install script that copies the rules into ~/.claude/rules; rejected because it leaves two copies.

title: Companion plugins are used when installed, reported when missing
summary: i-have-adhd, ponytail, mempalace and ECC each have a named step in the workflow; a missing one is reported once with its install command and never blocks work.
decision: The skill names the step where each companion is used and the fallback without it. The session-start hook lists the ones not installed.
reason: One broken or absent plugin should not stop all work.
alternatives: A hard requirement; copying their content into this repo.

title: Every project gets a dev-log
summary: Each project has a dev-log: numbered Markdown entries for decisions and milestones only, built into one HTML page by a builder copied into the project's tools folder.
decision: The dev-log kit from Total War Chess is the template: Markdown entries with id, date, status and title, a Python builder, a de-branded page and the legend theme. Entries are written for decisions, changes of direction, experiment results and milestones, not for routine tasks. The builder is copied into each project so it works by double-click and without Claude.
reason: Nothing told the story of why in a form worth reading.
alternatives: Markdown only; one builder kept inside the plugin; an entry for every task.

title: The notebook folder is asked for once per project
summary: Set-up asks where the human-facing notebook lives (docs/notebook by default, or an Obsidian vault) and stores the answer in the two tools config files.
decision: The location is a set-up question, never a guess. tools/record-config.json and tools/dev-log-config.json record it.
reason: Some projects keep their notebook in the repo and others in an Obsidian vault.
alternatives: Always docs/dev-log; always a notebook symlink.

title: HTML for the human, JSON for agents, one source of truth
summary: docs/record/*.json is the single source of truth, validated and cross-referenced by id; the human's HTML pages are generated from it and never edited.
decision: The owner asked for clean HTML for themselves and whatever parses best for agents, and left the design open. The record is three JSON arrays (record, roadmap, ideas) checked by tools/project_record.py; tools/build_record.py renders the notebook pages from them. Both use only the standard library.
reason: Two hand-written copies drift; one validated source with a generated view cannot.
alternatives: Markdown for both audiences; hand-written HTML with a separate JSON index.

title: No handover and no changelog; the record is a diary of decisions
summary: Handover and changelog are removed: git holds what changed, record.json holds decisions, reversals and open questions with one-line summaries, and board cards hold status and next steps.
decision: The project record is a diary of decisions, reversals and why. Each entry has a summary of at most 240 characters so an agent can skim the whole history through the digest. Where work stands lives in the note of its board card; questions for the owner are open entries; things noticed become issue cards or ideas.
reason: The handover got confusing, and five documents said overlapping things.
alternatives: Keeping the changelog as an agent-only file or as a page.

title: The roadmap is a board with a double-click launcher
summary: The roadmap is a kanban board the owner edits in the browser; open-roadmap.bat starts a localhost-only helper that writes card moves straight into roadmap.json.
decision: roadmap.html draws the cards. tools/roadmap_board.py serves the notebook on 127.0.0.1 with a random port and token, checks the Host header, validates every save against the whole record and refuses a save if the file changed on disk. Opened as a plain file the board is read-only.
reason: The owner wants to move cards themselves, and a browser page cannot save a file on its own.
alternatives: Picking the file in the browser each session (Chrome and Edge only); a static table.

title: Research is offered before major decisions and automatic for Research cards
summary: Before a major decision the agent asks whether to research it; a card in the board's Research column is researched at the next session without asking. The result is an HTML report plus an open entry.
decision: Rule 9 and RESEARCH.md. A report gives the short answer first, findings with sources, options side by side, each issue with ways round it, and what is still unknown. It ends in a question for the owner, never in a decision.
reason: Major decisions should rest on evidence the owner can read, not on what the agent already believed.
alternatives: Research always, without asking; research only on request; a background run the moment a card is dropped (IDEA-001).

title: Issues column holds known problems; nothing there is fixed unasked
summary: The board's Issues column lists known problems; agents file what they notice there but fix one only when asked or when its card is moved to To do.
decision: The owner asked for an issues area on the board. Agents add issue cards for problems they notice outside the task (rule 5) and leave them alone.
reason: Rule 5: change only what was asked. An issue list that fixes itself would grow every task's scope.
alternatives: Fixing issues automatically at session start, like Research cards.

title: The owner's writer's-voice file ships with the plugin
summary: The full writer's-voice file is published in the plugin and dev-log entries follow it; the Total War Chess banner art and entries are not included.
decision: skills/principles/writers-voice.md is the owner's file, unchanged. The page template is de-branded and uses the legend theme without artwork.
reason: Every project's dev-log should sound like its owner.
alternatives: A short list of voice rules only; a neutral theme.

title: The licence is MIT
summary: The repo is MIT-licensed: anyone may reuse it as long as the copyright notice stays.
decision: A LICENSE file with the MIT text, copyright emzakit, and the licence named in plugin.json.
reason: The repo is public; without a licence nobody else could legally reuse it.
alternatives: Another licence; no licence, leaving the code visible but not reusable.

title: This repo's notebook is docs/notebook, linked into the Obsidian vault
summary: This repo's notebook is docs/notebook, a link to the owner's Obsidian folder; it is ignored by git, so the pages and dev-log live in the vault, not in the repo.
decision: docs/notebook is a link to a folder in the owner's Obsidian vault. The owner made the link. The link is in .gitignore. Because this repo has no copy of the tools, its launchers run the template scripts with --config pointing at tools/record-config.json and tools/dev-log-config.json.
reason: The owner reads their notes in Obsidian, as with Total War Chess.
alternatives: A plain docs/notebook folder committed with the repo.

title: Set-up offers a notebook link into Obsidian
summary: The notebook's location stays the user's choice per project, and set-up always mentions the option of a link in the project that points into an Obsidian vault, as Total War Chess does.
decision: NOTEBOOK.md step 1 offers three choices: a folder in the project, a link in the project pointing elsewhere, or any other folder. It gives the command for a Windows junction and for a symbolic link, and says to ignore the link in git unless the pages should be committed. The configs hold the link's own path; the tools follow it.
reason: A link keeps the pages in Obsidian and the paths in the project short, and it is easy to miss.

title: Board cards carry a category, flags and links
summary: Cards get one coloured category, any number of flags and a list of links or file paths; the categories and flags live in board.json and the owner manages them from the board.
decision: roadmap.json cards gain the optional fields category, flags and links. docs/record/board.json holds the categories and flags with their colours; the starter set is Feature, UI, Bug, Refactor, Docs, Tooling and High, Medium, Low priority. A dialog on the board adds, renames, recolours and removes them. The digest shows each card's category, flags and links.
reason: The owner wants to sort and mark cards and to keep the files a card is about one click away.
alternatives: Free-text tags typed into the note; detecting links inside the note text.

title: The board opens only safe file types and shows everything else in its folder
summary: A card link opens only images, PDFs, text and media; folders, programs, web pages and office files are shown in their folder, network paths and symbolic links are refused, and the page never sends a path.
decision: The page asks the helper to open a link by card id, position and version; the helper reads the path from roadmap.json on disk. An allow-list decides what the system may open. Anything else, and every folder, is revealed in the file manager. Paths starting with two slashes and, on Windows, paths through a symbolic link are refused before the file system is touched.
reason: The independent tester and the security reviewer both showed that handing a folder to Windows to open runs a same-named script beside it, and that web pages and office files opened from a cloned repo can run script or leak credentials.
alternatives: Opening anything the system knows how to open; a deny-list of program types; opening folders with a trailing separator, which one reviewer could not prove safe.

title: Launchers and assets travel with the tools, for Windows, macOS and Linux
summary: The board and dev-log launchers live in tools/ as .bat, .command and .sh with no machine paths, and every build copies the theme and board script from tools/assets into the notebook.
decision: open-roadmap and rebuild-dev-log each come as .bat, .command and .sh in tools/ and find the scripts relative to themselves. The notebook's assets folder is generated from tools/assets on every build, so a fresh clone on any machine gets a working notebook from one launcher run. The launchers no longer live in the notebook folder and no path is filled in at set-up.
reason: The owner works on Windows and a Mac. A launcher holding one machine's path inside a synced notebook breaks on the other.
alternatives: Per-machine launchers generated into the notebook; one launcher per operating system kept in the notebook with paths filled in by hand.

title: Hooks run under bash and choose the interpreter once
summary: Each hook sets shell to bash and runs python3 if it works, else python, so the same hooks.json serves Windows, macOS and Linux without running a script twice.
decision: hooks.json commands are `py=python3; python3 -c '' 2>/dev/null || py=python; "$py" <script>` with "shell": "bash". Claude Code runs hooks in Git Bash on Windows.
reason: macOS has no `python` command by default, and a fallback that re-runs the script would hide a crash and lose the hook's input.
alternatives: `python … || python3 …`, which does not parse in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and runs twice on failure; a Node launcher, which adds a second runtime.

title: The record digest is treated as data, not instructions
summary: Everything the digest prints from the record is flattened to one line and cut at 300 characters, and the session-start hook says the digest is project data, because a cloned repo's record reaches the model's context.
decision: project_record.py cleans titles, notes, links, names and summaries before printing them. The hook caps error text at 1000 characters and labels the digest as data. A Research card shipped in a cloned repo is still researched without asking; that is how the feature works and is accepted.
reason: The security review put a fake system notice into the context through a card title with line breaks, and a 400 kB note through unchanged.
alternatives: Leaving the digest raw; refusing multi-line notes in the validator.
